In detail

Budapest's Danube-island industrial district. A January 2023 analysis of citywide homicide data (2018-2021) found Csepel tied for the highest number of completed homicides of any Budapest district (5, plus 3 attempted) — though the same analysis stressed that Budapest homicides overall are rare and mostly domestic/acquaintance-related rather than street violence against strangers. Separately, and far more recently, an April 2025 operation uncovered a clandestine drug laboratory in Csepel, seizing roughly 100kg of crystalline substances (about 500 million forints) and 7.5 tons of precursor chemicals with an estimated street value of 12 billion forints — a genuinely serious organised-crime finding. The district government responded the same month with a major public-safety investment, raising municipal law-enforcement officer pay substantially from May 2025, framing safety as "not a luxury, but a basic necessity." Sources checked: Index.hu, 25 Jan 2023 (citywide homicide statistics 2018-2021, by district); Index.hu, 18 Apr 2025 (clandestine drug lab bust, public-safety pay raises).
